name: GitHub Queue
author: Waveshare Widgets
description: Per repo: pull requests waiting on your review, and how the last workflow run finished. Uses conditional requests so it stays well inside the token's rate limit.

properties.name: repos
properties.label: Repositories
properties.help: One row per repository, as owner/name — the same text that appears in its URL. The token below must have access to every one of them.

properties.name: apiToken
properties.label: Personal access token
properties.placeholder: Fine-grained PAT with read access to the repos above
properties.help: A GitHub fine-grained personal access token (Settings → Developer settings → Tokens (fine-grained)). Give it access to the repositories listed above, then set three permissions to Read-only: Pull requests, for the review queue; Actions, for run status; and Metadata, which GitHub enables for you. Nothing here writes, so Read-only is the whole grant. A classic token also works — private repositories need the repo scope, public ones need none — but repo alone already grants write access to everything it covers.
